questions.q: Which customer service tasks should I automate?
questions.a: Automate the repetitive, predictable work. Good candidates are replies to common reviews, flagging high-risk reviews and negative trends, post-visit survey follow-ups, and basic questions about hours, directions and delivery status. These tasks gain the most from speed and consistency.

questions.q: What parts of customer service should stay human?
questions.a: Keep people on emotional recovery, escalations and brand voice moments. A real apology from a person lands better than a templated reply, and upset customers want to feel heard. Surprising a loyal guest or giving a social media shoutout also works best with a human behind it.

questions.q: How can I make automated replies sound more human?
questions.a: Use natural, conversational language instead of stiff scripts, and add context such as the location visited, the order or the feedback received. Make sure the AI escalates the right issues to the right people. Done well, automated replies should sound like your best team member.

questions.q: Why do multi-location brands need service automation?
questions.a: Across many locations, service can't depend on one standout manager. Labor shortages, rising service volumes and feedback scattered across platforms make consistency hard to achieve by hand. Automation handles the repetitive work so every location responds quickly and your team can focus on the relationship moments.

questions.q: How can Momos help automate guest service?
questions.a: Momos is an AI guest experience platform for multi-location restaurant brands. Its AI replies to reviews around the clock from a Unified Inbox, its AI agents answer guest messages, and it flags patterns in negative feedback so the right team can follow up. It also supports surveys and customer recovery.
